findings.summary: Passing-unit fixtures written as `test result: ok. 250 passed` will be read as units that did not finish and make failed_tests non-empty
findings.evidence: failed_test_names closes each `Running` section with `complete = self.failed == Some(self.listed.len())` (checks.rs:102), and failed_count reads `(\d+) failed` (checks.rs:166-170). A line `test result: ok. 250 passed` has no `N failed`, so failed stays None and `<binary> (did not finish)` is inserted (checks.rs:106-108). That breaks (d)'s `failed_tests` empty, and (f)'s `failed_tests == ["athena_core tests::a"]` and its `failing units: athena-core --lib` first line, because failing_units then lists every passing unit (client.rs:278-282). Fix: Write each passing unit's summary as cargo prints it: `test result: ok. 250 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`. Say so in the demonstration text.
findings.location: Demonstrations, criterion 2 (d) and (f); criterion 3 (d) and (e) reuse these logs

findings.summary: The plan does not say how the content forms match: start of line or anywhere in it
findings.evidence: The plan lists forms such as `Complete job`, `Removing includeIf` and `Evaluate and set job outputs` but does not say whether they match by starts_with or contains. failure_section also runs on local check output (checks.rs:618), so a contains match on a short phrase such as `Complete job` could cut real output. Fix: State that each content form matches by starts_with on the trimmed line, after an optional `##[group]` prefix is stripped, the same way the existing header check works (checks.rs:346-350).

summary: Read checks.rs (failure_section 373-419, failed_test_names 119-170, tests 821-949), gh/client.rs (failing_units, detail_from_job_logs 262-375), gh/tests.rs 380-772, xtask/src/shard.rs 255-339 and main.rs (step, error print), routing.rs 250-300 and 520-650, send_back.rs 280-421, verify.rs 55-88 and CHANGELOG.md 1-27. The plan's claims hold. failure_section cuts only at a cleanup header after an anchor and otherwise falls through to a plain tail. xtask prints `== shard k/n: <unit>` and `error: shard k of n: X of Y units failed: …` and keeps running units after one fails, so reducing the log to the failing unit from its own summary is grounded in output the log already holds, not a heuristic. No existing fixture has a `units failed:` summary. The existing tests (checks.rs 857/867/879/892/906/921, gh/tests.rs 494/578/607/674/726/746, routing.rs 593) still hold under the new cut, note and reserve rules as I traced them. The backward walk leaves a tail that a second pass does not cut. Every named seam exists with the needed visibility. CheckFailure::of has one production caller (run/checks.rs:453), as listed. No refusal rule or config field is added, and the work fits one producer run. Two minor fixture and spec details remain; neither blocks the design.
